sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-311.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD 311 was established by Ordinance No. 20306, passed by the Dallas City Council on May 10, 1989. Ordinance No. 20306 amended Ordinance Nos. 10962 and 19455, Chapters 51 and 51A of the Dallas City Code, as amended. Ordinance No. 20306 was amended by Ordinance No. 22602, passed by the Dallas City Council on November 8, 1995. (Ord. Nos. 10962; 19455; 20306; 22602; 25850)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-311.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 311 is established on property generally located at the northwest corner of Mockingbird Lane and West Lawther Drive. The size of PD 311 is approximately 19.4599 acres. (Ord. Nos. 20306; 22602; 25850)

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-311.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Definitions. Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51A apply to this article. In this article:

(1) ACCESSORY COMMUNITY CENTER means an accessory community center (private) as that use is defined in Chapter 51A, except that public meetings may be held at the center.

(2) HEIGHT means the vertical distance from mean sea level to the highest point of the structure.

(b) Interpretations.

(1) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this article are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51A.

(2) This district is considered to be a residential zoning district. (Ord. Nos. 20306; 25850; 25999; 29716)

SEC. 51P-311.103.1. EXHIBITS.

The following exhibits are incorporated into this article:

(1) Exhibit 311A: development plan.

(2) Exhibit 311B: topography and height zone plan. (Ord. 29716)

sections.title: Development Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-311.104. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

Development and use of the Property must comply with the development plan (Exhibit 311A). If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the development plan, the text of this article controls. (Ord. Nos. 20306; 25850; 25999; 29716)

SEC. 51P-311.104.2. TOPOGRAPHY AND HEIGHT ZONE PLAN.

Development and use of the Property must comply with the topography and height zone plan (Exhibit 311B). If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the topography and height zone plan, the text of this article controls. (Ord. 29716)

sections.title: Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-311.105. USES.

(a) The following uses are permitted on the Property:

(1) Adult day care facility.

(2) Convalescent and nursing homes, hospice care, and related institutions.

(3) Retirement housing.

(b) The following accessory uses are expressly permitted subject to the general provisions in Section 51A-4.217:

(1) Accessory community center.

(2) Office.

(3) Medical clinic or ambulatory surgical center. (Ord. Nos. 20306; 25850; 25999)

sections.title: Maximum Height
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-311.106. MAXIMUM HEIGHT.

(a) In general. Maximum structure height is as shown on the topography and height zone plan. The maximum structure height for each zone may not exceed the height shown for that zone and as listed below. Any changes or amendments to height zones on the development plan may not be considered as a minor amendment and shall follow the same procedures as a change in zoning district classification.

(b) Maximum height in height zones.

(1) In Zone 1, maximum structure height is 577 feet above sea level.

(2) In Zone 2, maximum structure height is 558 feet above sea level.

(3) In Zone 3, maximum structure height is as follows:

(i) In Zone 3B, 539 feet above sea level.

(ii) In Zone 3C, 549 feet above sea level.

(iii) In Zone 3D, 559 feet above sea level.

(4) In Zone 4, maximum structure height is as follows:

(i) In Zone 4B, 532 feet above sea level.

(ii) In Zone 4C, 540 feet above sea level.

(5) In Zone 5, maximum structure height is 577 feet above sea level.

(6) In Zone 6, maximum structure height is as follows:

(i) In Zone 6B, 547 feet above sea level.

(ii) In Zone 6C, 567 feet above sea level.

(iii) In Zone 6D, 577 feet above sea level.

(c) Projections. Structures listed in Section 51A-4.408(a)(2)(A) may project a maximum of 12 feet above the roofline or the maximum allowable structure height in that zone. (Ord. Nos. 20306; 25850; 25999; 29716)

sections.title: Setbacks
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-311.107. SETBACKS.

(a) Except as provided in this section, a 25 foot setback is required from all Property lines. Setbacks are not required for interior lots if the Property is subdivided.

(b) In Zones 3 and 4, for carport structures less than 15 feet in height above sea level, setbacks from the Property line are not required. (Ord. Nos. 20306; 25850; 29716)

sections.title: Density, Floor Area, And Lot Coverage
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-311.108. DENSITY, FLOOR AREA, AND LOT COVERAGE.

(a) Density. The combined maximum number of beds in the convalescent and nursing homes, hospice care, and related institutions, and dwelling units or suites in the retirement housing is 697.

(b) Floor area. Maximum floor area is 1,100,000 square feet.

(c) Lot coverage. Maximum lot coverage is 40 percent.

(d) Accessory structures.

(1) A maximum of five accessory structures may be located in the areas shown on the development plan (Exhibit 311B).

(2) An accessory structure may not exceed 18 feet in height above sea level.

(3) An accessory structure must be open on a minimum of two sides.

(4) An accessory structure may not exceed 1,500 square feet in floor area.

(5) An accessory structure must be a minimum of 150 feet from perimeter Property lines. (Ord. Nos. 20306; 25850; 25999; 29716)

sections.title: Off-Street Parking
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-311.109. OFF-STREET PARKING.

Off-street parking must be provided in accordance with the following table:

Number of Off-street Parking Use Spaces Required

Accessory community center One parking space per 200 square feet of floor area

Adult day care facility One parking space per 500 square feet of floor area

Convalescent and nursing One parking space per six beds homes, hospice care, and related institutions

Office One parking space per 333 square feet of floor area

Medical clinic or ambulatory One parking space per 200 square surgical center feet of floor area

Retirement housing One parking space per dwelling unit or suite (Ord. Nos. 20306; 25850; 25999)

sections.title: Screening, Landscaping, And Tree Preservation
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-311.110. SCREENING, LANDSCAPING, AND TREE PRESERVATION.

(a) Screening. A solid screening fence must be provided as shown on the development plan.

(b) Landscaping and tree preservation.

(1) Except as provided in this section, landscaping and tree preservation must comply with Article X. If there is a conflict between this section and Article X, this section controls.

(2) For purposes of complying with the requirements for artificial lot, required site trees may be planted anywhere in the district.

(c) Landscape plan. A landscape plan for an artificial lot that meets the following requirements must be submitted with each application for a building permit on the Property:

(1) One site tree, a minimum caliper of three inches, must be provided for each 4,000 square feet of land area in the artificial lot. Existing trees located in the artificial lot may count toward the site tree requirements if the existing trees are determined to be healthy by the building official.

(2) A surface parking space may not be located more than 120 feet from the trunk of a large canopy tree.

(3) Within the artificial lot, a minimum of two Section 51A-10.126 design standards must be provided. An existing site element may count as a design standard if the existing site element complies with a design standard listed in Section 51A-10.126.

(d) Perimeter landscape buffer strip. The perimeter landscape buffer strip requirements in Section 51A-10.125(b)(1) do not apply to the southwestern Property line or the western Property line adjacent to the DART line.

(e) Perimeter trees. For additions and new construction in Zones 3 and 4, one large tree is required for every 50 linear feet along the southwestern Property line and must be planted within 20 feet of the Property line. Perimeter trees are not required along the western Property line adjacent to the DART line.

(f) Street trees. The minimum number of street trees required along Mockingbird Lane may be planted within 150 feet of the Mockingbird Lane right-of-way, and must be planted between the buildings and the Mockingbird Lane right-of-way.

(g) Irrigation. Landscaping must be served by an automatic underground irrigation system.

(h) Maintenance. All plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. Nos. 20306; 25850; 25999; 29716)

SEC. 51P-311.110.1. DESIGN STANDARDS.

Exterior colors on lake facing facades constructed after April 22, 2015 are limited to earth tones, including tan, brown, and green. (Ord. 29716)

sections.title: Signs
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-311.111. SIGNS.

(a) Except as provided in this section, all signs must comply with the provisions for non- business zoning districts in Article VII.

(b) Signs may not exceed 12 square feet in effective area when attached to any structure or erected behind any building setback line.

(c) A maximum of two monument signs are permitted on the Property.

(1) Monument signs must be located a minimum of 10 feet from street rights-of-way.

(2) Maximum effective area for a monument sign is 150 square feet.

(3) Maximum height for a monument sign is five feet. (Ord. Nos. 20306; 25850; 29716)

sections.title: General Requirements
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-311.112. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS.

(a) Use of the Property must comply with the requirements of all applicable ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city.

(b) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the director of public works and transportation.

(c) The building official shall not issue a building permit or certificate of occupancy for a use in this PD until there has been full compliance with this article, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other applicable ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. Nos. 20306; 25850)
